# Sourdough Starter

The starter lives in a glass jar on the kitchen counter. I feed it every morning with equal weights of flour and water, discarding half first. In winter it takes eight hours to double, in summer four. A starter that smells of nail polish is hungry and needs feeding twice a day. Rye flour makes it more active than white flour.
Most of what I feed it is for the bread I bake on weekends: the dough rises on its strength, so a weak starter means a flat loaf.
